extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to Foundations of Computational Mathematics (Springer journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and manuscript-preparation guidelines for authors who wish to submit research articles to the journal Foundations of Computational Mathematics, covering file formats, content requirements, artwork, proofs, permissions, and editorial procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission route and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be sent to the Editors in Chief (jofocm@focm-society.org). Receipt of your submission will be acknowledged by email within one week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial submissions: send PDF for peer-review purposes. Expect an acknowledgement within one week. Follow the specified email address for initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred review file format (PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: For initial submissions PDF is the preferred format that will be used for peer-review purposes; upon acceptance you will be required to send the editable source files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a single PDF containing the entire manuscript (title page, author names, abstract, keywords, MSC numbers). Keep editable source files ready to supply after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required manuscript components
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission should include the entire manuscript with title page, author names, abstract, keywords, MSC numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure title page and all metadata are present in the initial PDF so reviewers and editors have full bibliographic and classification information.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX template optional but hyperref recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific LaTeX template is required; it is not necessary to use Springer Nature's LaTeX template for manuscript preparation, although including hyperlinks for the references is appreciated (add \usepackage{hyperref}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use their own style but should enable hyperref so references are reader-friendly in the compiled PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short cover letter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A short cover letter explaining (for non-experts) the relevance of the addressed computational problem and the foundational/original contributions of the manuscript should be added to the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the cover letter for a non-specialist editor/reviewer, highlighting originality and foundational impact rather than only technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of editable source files upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: While the PDF will be used for peer-review purposes, your source files will be transferred to the publisher for publication upon acceptance. Please ensure you provide all relevant editable source files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep LaTeX files, figures, and any other editable materials organized to submit promptly after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright transfer agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors will be required to sign a copyright transfer agreement in order for the article to be published. This form must accompany the final article sent to the Managing Editor. All of the authors of a manuscript must sign this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and complete the publisher's copyright transfer form for each author before final submission; delays may hold up publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for obtaining permissions to reprint previously published figures, tables, and other material. Letters of permission should accompany the final submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure and include written permission documents with the final files; do not assume fair use. Failure to provide permissions can block publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOI usage in references
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer-Verlag assigns a unique DOI to every article it publishes. It is important to include the DOI in references for articles published online where volume and page numbers are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include DOI strings for online-first articles in the reference list so citations resolve even before volume/page numbers are assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs turnaround and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Page proofs will be sent to the corresponding author for review and correction. Proofs should be returned within 48 hours. Articles may not be rewritten at the proof stage; only corrections of errors may be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for a quick proof check (48 hours). Limit changes to factual or typographical corrections; substantive rewrites are not permitted at proof stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement (English)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be written in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear and concise English to facilitate fair peer review. Consider professional editing if English is not your native language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering and shortened running title
rubrics_metrics.description: Every page should be consecutively numbered from the Title Page (1) on. A shortened version of the title that does not exceed 45 characters for use on page heading will be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number pages starting at title page as page 1. Provide a concise running head (≤45 characters) for headers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete author information and corresponding author
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete AUTHOR NAMES for each author, plus their mailing addresses and institutional affiliation and email addresses are required. The corresponding author must be clearly indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List full names, affiliations, postal addresses, and emails for all authors, and clearly mark which author is the corresponding author for proofs and editorial communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and format
rubrics_metrics.description: An ABSTRACT of reasonable length (we suggest not more than 200 words) in one paragraph that highlights the objectives, results, and conclusions of the paper is required. Do not cite figures, tables, or references within the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the abstract a single paragraph ≤200 words, focusing on aims, main results, and conclusions. Avoid citations and references to figures/tables in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS (MOS) subject classification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS (MOS) SUBJECT CLASSIFICATION NUMBERS are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate AMS subject classification codes to help editors and reviewers assign the manuscript to the correct area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list format and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: The REFERENCES to the literature should be listed alphabetically at the end of the manuscript following these examples. American Mathematical Society abbreviation style is also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete alphabetical reference list; follow the provided examples for books, chapters, and journal articles. Include DOIs where appropriate and use consistent abbreviation style.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-text citation numbering style
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the text of the articles, references should be identified by number within brackets; with the number of the reference in boldface type, with each reference in a set of brackets (unless sequential); e.g., [1], [2], [5]   [1-5]   [3, pp. 7-9].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bracketed numerical citations (boldface numbers) and ranges when sequential; ensure the reference numbers match the alphabetic reference list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table submission and legends
rubrics_metrics.description: TABLES should be submitted in separate files, with TABLE LEGENDS incorporated into the table files. Tables should have a clear and rational structure. All tables should be numbered. Provide enough information in legends so that each table is understandable without reference to the text. Every table should be cited in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit tables as separate files with self-contained legends and numbering; ensure each table is referenced in the main text and is understandable on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and file formats for illustrations (print)
rubrics_metrics.description: ILLUSTRATIONS should be of high quality, either professionally drawn or generated by graphics software. Submit figures as .eps or .tif files, in addition to hard copies. Graphics files should ONLY include the figures and their numbers/labels; there should be no extraneous information included, e.g., captions, author names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide separate EPS or TIFF files containing only the artwork and labels; supply accompanying figure legends in the text file. Do not embed captions or author info in figure files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure legends and no scanned figure submission
rubrics_metrics.description: FIGURE LEGENDS should be incorporated into the text files. Do not submit scans of hard copy figures. Hard copies of figures must be submitted along with hard copy of the manuscript. The hard copy of each figure must be labeled on its back, indicating figure number, author name, and an indication of the top of the figure where necessary. Figures (hard copy) should be submitted at their final size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide figure legends inside the manuscript text; if supplying hard-copy figures, label their backs clearly and send at final size. Avoid submitting scans as primary artwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color and black & white printing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations will be printed in black and white only in the journal. See instructions for color illustrations and other ancillary materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare figures so they remain interpretable when converted to grayscale; consult color-figure instructions if color reproduction is desired (extra charges or online-only may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of ancillary materials (video, datasets, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Video, illustrations, data sets, etc. may be submitted for online publication with your article. These materials are subject to review and approval of the Editorial staff, and should be included with article submission. Preferred formats are: Video .mov; Illustrations .gif, .jpg, or .pdf. If another format is used, a free viewer for that format must be available on the Internet for download.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include ancillary materials at submission for consideration; prefer the listed formats and ensure any nonstandard format can be viewed with freely available software.

rubrics_metrics.name: File size restrictions for ancillary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Files should be kept as small as possible. File size restrictions are 2MB per file and 10MB per article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress or reduce resolution where acceptable to meet the 2MB per-file and 10MB per-article limits; large supplementary datasets may need to be hosted elsewhere or submitted with prior agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for electronically produced illustrations for print (vector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector (line) Graphics exported from a drawing program should be stored in EPS format. Suitable drawing program: Adobe Illustrator. For simple line art the following drawing programs are also acceptable: Corel Draw, Freehand, Canvas. No rules narrower than .25 pt. No gray screens paler than 15% or darker than 60%. Screens meant to be differentiated from one another must differ by at least 15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide vector artwork as EPS from recommended programs, respect minimum line thickness (.25 pt) and gray-scale contrast rules to ensure reproducible print quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spreadsheet/presentation graphics not acceptable for print
rubrics_metrics.description: Most presentation programs (Excel, PowerPoint, Freelance) produce data that cannot be stored in an EPS format. Therefore graphics produced by these programs cannot be used for print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recreate charts and plots in proper vector/graphics software that can export EPS for print-quality results rather than submitting PowerPoint/Excel graphics for print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone, scanned image and resolution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Black & white and color illustrations should be saved in TIFF format. Scanned reproductions of black and white photographs should be provided as 300 ppi TIFF files. Scanned color illustrations should be provided as TIFF files scanned at a minimum of 300 ppi with a 24-bit color depth. Line art should be provided as TIFF files at 600 ppi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the specified ppi and bit-depths for scanned images to ensure print clarity; prefer original art when possible as printers have high-quality scanners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics from videos for print
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate files should be prepared for frames from a video that are to be printed in the journal. When preparing these files you should follow the same rules as listed under Halftone Illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract and prepare still frames from video according to halftone TIFF and resolution guidelines if any frames are to appear in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for electronically produced illustrations for online (video)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quicktime (.mov) is the preferred format, but .rm, .avi, .mpg, etc. are acceptable. No video file should be larger than 2MB. To decrease the size of your file, consider changing frame speed, number of colors/greys, viewing size (in pixels), or compression. Video is subject to Editorial review and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit online-video materials in preferred formats and within the 2MB size limit; reduce resolution or frame rate if necessary. Expect editorial approval for online materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of editing services and language support
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature Author Services can help with English language editing, developmental comments, manuscript formatting, figure preparation, translation, and more. Use of these tools, or any other service, is not a requirement for publication, nor does it imply or guarantee acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider professional language/editing services if English needs substantial work. The publisher's copyeditors will check spelling and formal style after acceptance but substantial pre-submission editing may help peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special guidance for authors from China/Japan/Korea
rubrics_metrics.description: For authors from China/Japan/Korea the page lists recommended editing services (e.g., Edanz) and notes that language polishing is helpful but not required or a basis for acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors from these regions may consult the recommended local-language resources for editorial services; use is voluntary and not a guarantee of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access information
rubrics_metrics.description: To find out more about publishing your work Open Access in Foundations of Computational Mathematics, including information on fees, funding and licences, visit the Open access publishing page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the journal's open access page for APCs, licensing options, and funding information if you wish to publish OA.
